analysis:
Examined both BASE workflow excerpts and the complete bounded patch. The only executable change sets DARKBLOOM_RELEASE_ENVIRONMENT=prod for qualify-sdk (.github/workflows/release-provider.yml, HEAD 239–242); the build-job comment is also corrected. This explicitly selects production defaults for qualification tests while build-provider retains lane-specific defaults (BASE 178–198). No supported authorization, credential-exposure, encryption, billing or availability regression follows from this change alone. Source verification, successful build/qualification prerequisites, signing and entitlement checks, notarization, final archived-artifact checks and retained publication identity remain unchanged in the supplied ranges (BASE 133–164, 254–258, 588–666, 729–962). These remain relevant to A-011/A-017, TB-011, T-013 and T-054; the change does not itself grant serving permission or establish runtime secrecy.
Integration must reconcile the new job environment with the local provider-release-build action's qualification lane and environment input (BASE 247–250), and Package.swift's environment selection. Their implementations are not supplied: whether the input overrides the job environment, and whether production-default tests still exercise the intended lane qualification contract, remain unverified. The supplied workflow alone does not establish a missing control. No cache-storage or request-path changes are visible; T-041's controls are not revalidated by this source pass.
